chains.title: TCF7L2 enhancer effect on POU5F1B

links.claim: The chain hypothesis is that TCF7L2 binds this element more strongly on alt C. TCF7L2 is selected because it has HCT116 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant and is highly expressed in HCT116 (rank 53 of 1626 TFs), whereas many other listed bound TFs are supported only in other biosamples. No QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific ChIP/reporter data is supplied for TCF7L2, so the alt>C direction is unmeasured.

The variant lies in cCRE EH38E3858447 (pELS) with DNase, H3K27ac and CTCF signal, so it is in an enhancer-like element; these are ENCODE maxima, not HCT116-specific or allele-specific activity measurements.

POU5F1B is the nearest protein-coding gene and the variant is in a POU5F1B intron; L2G also favors POU5F1B, but the L2G sets are non-CRC with PIP 0.04, colon eQTLs are absent, and E21 shows POU5F1B is not a colorectal dependency. Target assignment is therefore plausible but unproven.
HCT116 is the supplied colorectal carcinoma context and has TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant plus high TCF7L2 expression.

If causal, allele-specific TCF7L2 binding at this enhancer would alter POU5F1B expression and contribute to 8q24 colorectal cancer; the chain's stated direction is increased POU5F1B, but the sign is unproven and TCF7L2 could repress. Direct support is absent: no GWAS Catalog association for rs73706717, no colon eQTL, and POU5F1B is not a colorectal-lineage dependency. E18 is gene-level literature, not variant-specific.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or enhancer reporter assays show stronger TCF7L2 binding and stronger enhancer activity for alt C than ref T.
TCF7L2 knockdown or CRISPR disruption of EH38E3858447 changes POU5F1B expression in HCT116.
The variant shows an allele-specific effect on POU5F1B but not on MYC.

Colon eQTL or 3C/CRISPR evidence links this variant to MYC rather than POU5F1B.

chains.title: SP1 enhancer effect on POU5F1B

links.claim: The chain hypothesis is that SP1 binds this element more strongly on alt C. SP1 is selected because it has HCT116 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant and is expressed in HCT116 (rank 118 of 1626 TFs). No QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific ChIP/reporter data is supplied for SP1, so the alt>C direction is a motif-based hypothesis, not a measured allelic effect.
The variant lies in the active pELS EH38E3858447, a proximal enhancer-like element with DNase and H3K27ac signal; the annotation is not HCT116-specific or allele-specific.

POU5F1B is the nearest protein-coding gene and the variant is in a POU5F1B intron; L2G favors POU5F1B but with non-CRC sets and PIP 0.04, colon eQTLs are absent, and E21 shows POU5F1B is not a colorectal dependency. The enhancer-gene link is therefore weak.
HCT116 is the supplied colorectal carcinoma context and has SP1 occupancy over the variant plus SP1 expression.

The chain posits that SP1-mediated enhancer activity increases POU5F1B expression and contributes to colorectal cancer biology, but there is no GWAS Catalog association for rs73706717, no colon eQTL, and no variant-specific SP1/POU5F1B assay; E18 is gene-level literature.

chains.title: TCF7L2 enhancer effect on MYC

links.claim: The chain hypothesis is that TCF7L2 binds this element more strongly on alt C. TCF7L2 has HCT116 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant and is highly expressed in HCT116, but no QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific ChIP/reporter data is supplied, so the alt>C direction is unmeasured. Other listed TFs such as CTCF, CEBPB and MYBL2 are bound only in other biosamples, which is why TCF7L2 is preferred over them.
The variant is in the pELS EH38E3858447, an active enhancer-like element by DNase and H3K27ac annotation; the evidence is ENCODE-wide, not HCT116-specific or allelic.

MYC is a canonical 8q24 colorectal cancer target 334 kb upstream, and E19 names a colorectal cancer-associated MYC-335 enhancer in this region, but that study characterized rs67491583, not rs73706717. No 3C/CRISPR/eQTL evidence shows this element contacts MYC, and POU5F1B is closer and in the variant-containing transcript.
HCT116 has TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant and high TCF7L2 expression, but this does not establish a broader 8q24-active cell context or allele-specific activity.

The chain posits that allele-specific TCF7L2 binding increases MYC expression and contributes to colorectal cancer, but there is no GWAS Catalog association for rs73706717, no colon eQTL, and no variant-specific MYC regulatory assay; E18 is generic MYC/ecDNA literature.
